entries.title: Georgetown Falls Short Against Texas, Losing 92-83
entries.summary: Jaland Lowe scored 21 points for the previously undefeated Hoyas. Kayvaun Mulready had 18 and Vincent Iwuchukwu and Elmarco Jackson 17 apiece.
entries.content:
SAN DIEGO — Isaiah Johnson scored 26 points and Marcus Spears Jr. added 18 for No. 7 Texas, which beat Georgetown 92-83 Thursday in the Rady Children’s Invitational with minimal help from 7-foot center Matas Vokietaitis.

The Longhorns (7-0) played the final 9:30 without Vokietaitis after he was whistled for his fifth foul, a technical. He had only five points and one rebound in 13 minutes after coming in leading Texas with 20.7 points and 8.8 rebounds.

Joe Sterling had 14 points and David Punch had 11 points and 10 rebounds for the Longhorns (7-0), who will play in Friday’s championship game against St. Mary’s, an 85-70 winner over No. 6 UCLA.

Jaland Lowe scored 21 points for the Hoyas (6-1). Kayvaun Mulready had 18 and Vincent Iwuchukwu and Elmarco Jackson 17 apiece.

Texas was up 70-58 when Vokietaitis was whistled for a technical. Lowe made both free throws and then hit two more on the ensuing possession to pull the Hoyas to 70-62.

Sterling then hit his third straight 3-pointer in a 2 1/2-minute stretch to push the Texas lead to 73-62.

The Hoyas got it to single digits in the final four minutes, but the Longhorns responded each time. Spears had a slam dunk for an 81-71 lead with 4 minutes to go and Johnson hit a dagger 3-pointer with 1:26 left to make it 90-78.

The Hoyas pulled to 45-39 on Mulready’s 3-pointer early in the second half before the Longhorns went on a 14-2 run, keyed by seven points from Spears.

Texas was tested in the first half when Georgetown twice had a four-point lead, but closed with a 15-3 run for a 41-30 halftime edge.

The Longhorns also had a 14-2 run early in the second half to open a 59-41 lead.

Texas outrebounded Georgetown 45-24, which helped the Longhorns overcome 19 turnovers.

Up Next

Texas: Faces St. Mary’s in the tournament title game on Friday.

Georgetown: Faces No. 6 UCLA in the third-place game on Friday.

entries.title: Hackers Breach the Air Force’s Cloud Computing Program: Report
entries.summary: The attack put sensitive military data, including for logistics and tactical operations, at risk.
entries.content:
The Air Force’s cloud computing program was hacked earlier this year, potentially putting sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data at risk, according to a report from Reuters.

The breach occurred during a system upgrade at Cloud One within the past month or so, Reuters reported, adding that the outlet could not establish the identity of the hackers, the scope of the intrusion, or whether any data had been stolen.

The Air Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Washington Sun.

A Pentagon official told The Sun it does not comment on the status of its networks “as a matter of policy and operations security.”

Launched in 2017, Cloud One is the Air Force’s leading provider of state-of-the-art cloud computing platforms, technologies, approaches and solutions, according to its website. It runs on Microsoft, Oracle, Amazon and Google technology.

The tech companies have yet to publicly comment on the reported breach.

The Air Force describes Cloud One as a “one-stop shop for Department of Defense mission application owners that require a full array of commercial cloud services, delivering speed, scale and security with cutting-edge technologies, approaches and solutions for cloud computing.”

According to Reuters, Cloud One hosts the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control, a program that collects defense radar data, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, a bomb-tracking and missile service.

The news outlet cited anonymous sources to report the hacking caused disruption to military services, barring updates to Cloud One applications and stopping officials from migrating back-office applications to Cloud One.

One source told Reuters that hackers reached Cloud One’s control plane, which it compared to a universal remote.

The hacking comes after a slew of technology outages over the last month impacting air travel, Microsoft Outlook and banks.

The U.S. government has also suffered a recent string of cyber incidents that affected the U.S. intelligence community, the FBI, the Pentagon and the departments of Homeland Security and Treasury.

entries.title: Georgetown Can't Keep Up With No. 6 UCLA in 75-63 Loss
entries.summary: The Hoyas fell in the third-place game at the Rady Children's Invitational in San Diego.
entries.content:
SAN DIEGO — Sophomore guard Azavier Robinson scored a career-high 23 points off the bench for No. 6 UCLA, which rebounded from its first loss of the season to beat Georgetown 75-63 Friday in the third-place game at the Rady Children's Invitational on Friday.

Eric Dailey Jr. added 14 while Jaylen Petty and Xavier Booker had 10 apiece for UCLA (7-1).

The Bruins played more aggressively than they did on Thursday, when they had the lead just once and allowed 15 3-pointers in an 85-70 loss to Saint Mary’s.

UCLA took the lead on Dailey's 3-pointer less than four minutes in and never surrendered it.

Robinson made consecutive shots early in the first half, the second one off a steal. He had another steal for an easy score midway through the second half. He got a nice ovation as he was subbed out for a breather with the Bruins leading 71-59 with 2:27 to play.

Robinson's previous career high was 15 against Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Nov. 11.

The Bruins forced the Hoyas into poor shooting from early on. The Hoyas made only 6 of 23 shots in the first half for 26.1%, and just 18 of 52 overall for 34.6%.

UCLA shot only 36.1% in the first half and finished at 40.6 percent, but the Bruins outrebounded the Hoyas 43-32

Elmarco Jackson scored 13 for Georgetown (6-2) while Kayvaun Mulready and Caleb Williams had 11 each.

The Hoyas lost 92-83 to No. 7 Texas on Thursday.
entries.author: The Associated Press
